decision.trend: Research has been focused on understanding the effects of short-range order (SRO) and precipitation on the thermal and mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys (HEAs). Studies have shown that SRO can enhance the strength and stability of HEAs, while precipitation can improve their thermal conductivity. However, the relationship between SRO, precipitation, and thermal conductivity is still not well understood.
decision.unsolved: The optimal material for lattice heat conductivity in the presence of SRO precipitates is still unknown. Further research is needed to understand the effects of SRO and precipitation on the thermal conductivity of HEAs and to identify the most promising materials for this application.
decision.why: Precipitation engineering has been shown to be a effective way to improve the thermal conductivity of HEAs. By controlling the size, shape, and distribution of precipitates, it may be possible to optimize the thermal conductivity of HEAs in the presence of SRO precipitates. This approach has the potential to lead to the development of new materials with improved lattice heat conductivity.
